item.content:encoded: I remember reading this before I even had an account and wishing that I could +1 it. Today, my wish has been granted.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Sir, this is the most goddamned hysterical thing I've ever read on this site. It took me over thirty minutes to read, simply because I was in laughing fits the entire time. You are a beautiful person for making this. +1

(Now, while the entire thing was totally awesome, I do have one complaint with the ending being a little lackluster. It certainly made me laugh, but when compared to the rest of the piece, it was getting pretty close to a BK-Class.)

item.content:encoded:
Now, noodles are good usually, but I never really liked the special ones because my dad walked out when I was ten—

I didn't notice this the first time I read it. :|

Oh man, I really liked this. Enjoyable read. How did I not upvote this yet aaaaaa

I like the dialogue in particular. "Nobody works on Bender's Day. The laws of physics take a break on Bender's Day. Relax. I brought you your coffee, just the way you like it: 'Doctor Patil's Favorite Drink', Very Fine." Teehee.

Upvoted.

item.content:encoded:
Then by all means continue to hate it!

EDIT: That was ridiculously passive-aggressive, damn! Sorry!

For anyone else who was turned off by the aggressive goofiness of this tale, you might prefer the earlier draft! It's a fair bit less silly, and has a whole subplot where Patil is questioning the messed up cartoonish nature of reality that was cut from this. If you're interested, and you're also a big fan of super long half-finished drafts, check it out!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I guess the point was to evoke the wacky senior staff stuff from the earlier days of the site, so in that I suppose you succeeded. Still, there's a reason that "lolfoundation" became something of a pejorative term around here. This is so aggressively over the top and in-jokey that it became tiresome extremely quickly. -1.

item.content:encoded:
She ran off stage, clawing at he eyes and shrieking.

Only lil thing I saw, should be 'her', right?

Other than that, yes, the ending is not 'gratuitous', it was quite clear they were all going to end up dead XD

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: The ending caught me off guard, but not in a bad way. Have an upvote.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Fair enough! Hope it didn't seem completely unjustified — I tried to hint pretty strongly that something like that was going to happen, especially with that specific SCP.

I don't like gratuitous "everybody dies" endings either, but I did have a purpose behind using one. As the misuse of SCPs got more and more blatant, there was only really one way it could end.
